title: Canonical entity mart for workspace + feature telemetry (fast ad-hoc and cost attribution)
creator: Raj Patel
description:
Problem: Current Console analytics are spread across many event streams and denormalized views. Ad-hoc BI queries are slow, cost attribution for routes/features is brittle, and product/finance teams lack a single canonical source for workspace-level feature usage and token costs.

Goal: Build a canonical, query-optimized entity mart that consolidates per-invocation telemetry (route/chat/generation/embedding) into a tenant- and workspace-centric schema plus time-windowed materialized snapshots to power low-latency dashboards, fast ad-hoc exploration, and deterministic cost attribution. The mart must support incremental refresh, clear lineage, and data contracts for downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical entity mart tables (workspace_entity, feature_usage_facts, invocation_dimensions) defined and documented in the data catalog
End-to-end transformation pipeline implemented in dbt/airflow with incremental runs; daily and hourly snapshots available
Query performance: common dashboard queries return < 2s for 30-day tenant slices in prod replica cluster
Cost attribution accuracy validated against sample billing data within 5% for P0 tenants (sample set)
Lineage links created to raw event topics, CDC sources, and GitHub PRs; data contracts published to the contract registry
Backfill strategy and safety checks implemented; backfill completed for last 12 months of production telemetry
tasks: Schema design: define canonical dimension keys (workspace_id, tenant_id, user_id, feature_id, model_variant) and consistent naming conventions
Transformation logic: implement aggregation to feature_usage_facts (invocations, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, errors) from raw invocation events
Materialized snapshots: implement hourly rolling snapshots and weekly 7-day rollups using partitioned materialized views
Incremental pipeline: build dbt models with unique keys and idempotent merges; wire into existing Airflow DAGs
SLA tests: add QA queries to monitor freshness, row-count delta tests, and schema drift alerts
Cost mapping: join invocation facts to price profiles (by model_variant + quantization profile) and validate against billing exports
Backfill plan: create safe-window backfill job with throttling and tombstone handling for deleted workspaces
Observability: add tracing tags for pipeline runs and push ingestion metrics to Prometheus/Grafana dashboards
Docs & contracts: publish Confluence spec, data catalog entries, and a short consumer-facing README with example SQL
Rollout: pilot with product analytics and finance teams; collect feedback and iterate
data_model_notes: Dimension pattern: skinny lookup tables for workspace, tenant, feature, model_variant to avoid repeated JSON payloads
Fact grain: one row per invocation_id with standardized duration and token metrics; pre-aggregated daily/hourly rollups for fast scans
Partitions: time-based partitioning on event_timestamp and workspace_id secondary clustering for high-activity tenants
Storage: compressed columnar tables (e.g., Snowflake/BigQuery) plus a hot replica in our analytical Postgres for sub-second dashboard queries
Lineage: include raw_event_topic, source_offset, and ingestion_run_id fields on facts for reproducibility
